questions.q: In the food chain oak leaves → caterpillar → blue tit → sparrowhawk, which is the secondary consumer?
questions.why: Producer, then primary consumer (caterpillar), then secondary consumer (blue tit).

questions.q: Which process in the carbon cycle removes carbon dioxide from the atmosphere?
questions.why: Photosynthesis takes in CO₂; respiration, combustion and decomposition release it.

questions.q: Why do food chains usually have fewer than five trophic levels?
options: Energy is lost at each level, so too little is left for higher levels.
Energy is recycled at each trophic level.
Top predators eat all the producers.
Carbon is lost from the food chain.
questions.why: Energy is lost at each transfer (respiration, heat, faeces, uneaten parts).

questions.q: State two undesirable effects of deforestation.
questions.model: Any two: reducing biodiversity; extinction; loss of soil; flooding; increase of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere.
points: two from: reduced biodiversity, extinction, loss of soil, flooding, more CO₂ in the atmosphere
